name: GraphQL
description: A query language for APIs where clients ask for exactly the fields they need in a single request.

name: Microservices
description: Splitting an application into small, independently deployable services that talk over the network.

name: Real-time Architecture
description: Event streaming (e.g. Kafka) that moves data between systems as it happens instead of in batches.

name: Search
description: Inverted-index engines (e.g. Elasticsearch) for fast full-text and faceted queries.

name: Serverless
description: Run functions on demand without managing servers; you pay per invocation.

name: Object Storage
description: Flat, massively scalable blob storage (e.g. S3) addressed by key.

name: Caching
description: Keep hot data in fast memory (e.g. Redis) to cut latency and database load.

name: Load Balancer
description: Spreads incoming traffic across many servers for scale and availability.

name: CDN
description: Edge servers worldwide that cache static content close to users.

name: Message Queue
description: Decouples producers and consumers with durable, asynchronous messages.

name: SQL Database
description: Relational storage with schemas, joins and ACID transactions.

name: NoSQL Database
description: Schema-flexible stores (document, key-value, wide-column) built to scale out.

name: Sharding
description: Partitioning data across many database nodes by a shard key.

name: Rate Limiting
description: Caps how many requests a client can make in a time window.

name: API Gateway
description: Single entry point that routes, authenticates and throttles API calls.

name: Kubernetes
description: Orchestrates containers: scheduling, scaling, healing and rollout.

name: Observability
description: Logs, metrics and traces that let you understand a running system.

name: Consistent Hashing
description: Maps keys to nodes so adding/removing nodes moves minimal data.
